transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Alex Chen (Brightline Platform), Maria Lopez (Brightline ML Eng), Tara Singh (Brightline Security), Derek Moore (Brightline PM)

00:00 Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we will go into the bench numbers Priya pulled.
00:10 Alex Chen: Hey Jordan, hi Priya, Alex here. We got Maria, Tara, Derek on.
00:15 Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya from Redwood. I have the run outputs ready.
00:20 Derek Moore: Morning, thanks.
00:30 Jordan Kim: Okay great. Agenda: onboarding status, access blockers, bench results, tuning proposals, and next steps. If anything else pop up please flag.
01:05 Maria Lopez: Quick context — our goal for the pilot is to hit sub-200ms p50 and sub-800ms p95 on typical clinical summarization prompts at 1k token windows, and also ramp to 30 qps for stress.
01:35 Priya Nair: Got it. The baseline runs we did were single-region hosted on a g4-like equivalent with quantized model variant. We measured latency with (inaudible) and also ran a small synthetic traffic to mimic your 40% long sequences.
02:10 Jordan Kim: Before we dive numbers, onboarding updates? Alex?
02:18 Alex Chen: Two blockers. One — VPC peering hasn't been set up; we sent the petition to infra but waiting on a CIDR confirmation. Two — service account key rotation policy in our org prevents us from long-lived keys; we need either a short-term key or an OIDC flow.
02:40 Samir Patel: Noted. We usually support short-lived tokens via OIDC if you want—our Private offering supports that, and Dedicated can be integrated via VPC peering.
02:55 Tara Singh: For security we need KMS integration and confirmation about whether logs will include raw prompts. We cannot have PHI in logs.
03:10 Priya Nair: Understood — Redwood has an option to redact prompts at the ingestion side, and for Dedicated/Private logs can be fully controlled by customer's logging pipeline. We'll send the doc.
03:30 Derek Moore: Cool. Now the numbers?
03:40 Priya Nair: Yes. So initial run — p50 185ms, p95 1.2s, average token generation ~40ms/token. But that p95 is higher than expected because of cold KV cache on multi-turn prompts. The workload had 25% multi-turn. When we enabled KV-cache prefix hits we saw p95 drop to around 760ms.
04:20 Maria Lopez: Wait, the first run without KV cache gave 1.2s p95 — we thought Redwood's hosted numbers would be closer to what you advertise. Any idea why it's spiking?
04:35 Priya Nair: A couple of reasons — quantization mode, sequence length skew, and batching. The initial test used batch size 8 to optimize throughput; that pushed a tail on latency. Also some GPU kernel choice forced emulation for attention for longer seqs — we'll need to pin a different kernel path.
05:05 Jordan Kim: Also note you were on the generic quantized profile; we have a recommend q4f16 profile for your model family that trades a few points of perplexity for much lower memory and slightly faster kernels.
05:30 Maria Lopez: Could that materially change p95?
05:34 Priya Nair: Yes, we saw improvements ~15–25% on p95 in similar runs. But to be safe, we'll run a second baseline with KV cache on, batch size 1 and the q4f16 profile.
05:50 Alex Chen: Sounds good. Another question — you mentioned Dedicated earlier. If we pick Dedicated, will that reduce our p95 significantly?
06:05 Jordan Kim: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbors and gives guaranteed slots and lower variance; in our benchmarks Dedicated often reduces p95 by ~10–30% depending on load shape, but it's usage/commit tradeoff. Pricing will reflect reserved capacity.
06:30 Derek Moore: We have budget questions. Send the Dedicated vs hosted delta with region options.
06:35 Jordan Kim: Will do.
06:45 Priya Nair: Back to tuning — we recommend three steps: 1) enable KV cache/prefix caching for multi-turn, 2) drop batching down for p95-sensitive routes to 1–2, 3) switch quant profile to q4f16 or try half-precision on Dedicated. We'll script the bench.
07:10 Maria Lopez: For the KV cache, any extra infra or config we need to run on our side?
07:20 Priya Nair: No extra infra — it's managed in the runtime. You just need to indicate the prefix tokens in the request metadata. We'll share the sample wrapper.
07:35 Alex Chen: Can you share the sample code? We had trouble with tokenization mismatch in prior runs with other vendors.
07:45 Priya Nair: Absolutely — I'll share the wrapper and tokenization sanity tests. The repo link is in the doc we uploaded: https://redwood.ai/pilot-resources/tokenization-checks (note: example link).
08:00 Tara Singh: Regarding compliance, can you confirm where logs are stored for Hosted vs Dedicated, and what the retention policy is?
08:10 Jordan Kim: Hosted: logs retained in Redwood-managed storage for 30 days by default, can be configured. Dedicated: logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoint or retained per contract. We'll send the exact SOC2 scope.
08:30 Maria Lopez: Do we have to mask PHI at the client side or will Redwood redact before logs persist?
08:40 Priya Nair: We offer both: client-side redaction recommended; we also have server-side redaction rules that can be applied, but for compliance customers typically control it on their side or run Private.
09:00 Alex Chen: Ok. Any networking specifics — MTU, TCP idle timeouts etc. we should be aware of for VPC peering?
09:10 Priya Nair: Our docs list recommended MTU 1500, and keep-alive of 30s for long-running KV streams. We'll paste those in the infra checklist.
09:22 Jordan Kim: I'll attach the infra checklist after the call.
09:30 Priya Nair: Now I'll walk through the bench pdf. Summary: baseline run A (batch 8, no kv) — p50 185ms, p95 1.2s. Run B (batch 1, kv warm) — p50 160ms, p95 760ms. Run C (Dedicated-sim mode with half-precision) — p50 145ms, p95 520ms, but note that Dedicated-sim uses reserved compute so it's not perfectly apples-to-apples.
10:10 Maria Lopez: That Dedicated-sim improvement seems attractive. Do you have the exact script to reproduce Run B?
10:18 Priya Nair: Yes — script, Dockerfile, and the dataset sample will be in the bench artifact: https://redwood.ai/pilot-resources/bench-2025-11-05 (placeholder link). We'll also include the config flags for kv and batch size.
10:35 Alex Chen: We noticed occasional 5xx errors at high QPS spike. Any idea?
10:45 Priya Nair: We saw transient queue saturation on the control plane when bursts exceeded the configured concurrency. For Hosted we can tune autoscale thresholds and burst capacity; Dedicated gives steadier concurrency. We'll also adjust client-side retry/backoff.
11:08 Derek Moore: About autoscale — what are reasonable thresholds to avoid those spikes?
11:15 Priya Nair: We recommend keeping sustained qps within 70–80% of provisioned throughput and tuning the burst buffer to handle short spikes. We'll provide recommended policies based on your traffic profile.
11:40 Jordan Kim: Any competitors or in-house options you're evaluating?
11:45 Alex Chen: We're looking at Anthropic and a small internal self-hosted eval. Security team is also poking at OpenAI for compliance and cost. But your metrics and tooling around rollouts are a strong point.
12:00 Tara Singh: Security: specific ask — can you provide an example SOC2 report and a network flow diagram for Private?
12:10 Jordan Kim: Yes, we'll drop the SOC2 redacted PDF and a Private deployment diagram; expect that in the doc drop.
12:25 Maria Lopez: On the perf side, how do you recommend we instrument telemetry so we can attribute tail latency to model vs infra?
12:35 Priya Nair: We expose per-token timing and stage timings (tokenize, generation, kv lookup, kernel execution). We'll share the trace integration; it maps onto your existing tracing via headers.
12:50 Alex Chen: Good. One more infra question — do you support pinning a model version so we can run a canary?
12:55 Samir Patel: Yes, rollouts and canary policies are standard — you can pin to a model version and configuration for deterministic runs.
13:10 Derek Moore: Alright, recap and next steps please.
13:20 Jordan Kim: Recap — blockers: VPC peering + service account key rotation. Priya will run a second bench with kv enabled, batch size 1, and q4f16 and share results. I will send Dedicated vs Hosted pricing and region availability. Samir will send onboarding checklist + infra config. Customer to confirm CIDR and test OIDC option for short-lived tokens. Compliance doc drop for SOC2 and logging.
13:50 Maria Lopez: Sounds right. Timeline expectations?
14:00 Jordan Kim: We'll aim to send quote and bench artifacts by 2025-11-08; bench rerun artifacts by 2025-11-07.
14:12 Alex Chen: Good. One last nit — earlier transcriber noted 'KV cache' as 'K V cache' sometimes in our notes; small thing, ignore.
14:20 Jordan Kim: Noted. Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with the artifact links.
14:30 Meeting ended.
